ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p519/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p519/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p519/r3.claim: Despite his opponents’ disgust, the Prophet must declare that he invokes God alone and ascribes no partners to Him, even when they assign those partners a share with God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p519/r3.anchor: he will invoke God alone and not ascribe partners to Him, even though they might regard these partners to have a great share

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p301/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p301/r5.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p301/r5.claim: They understand قال إنما أدعو as the Prophet saying to his hostile crowd that he worships God alone, which does not justify their unified enmity; he may instead be speaking to amazed jinn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p301/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: قال إنما أدعوا ربي: أي أعبده، أي قال للمتظاهرين عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p301/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p301/r6.speaker: الجن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p301/r6.claim: Another interpretation makes the jinn themselves quote the Prophet's words to their people; which reading fits depends on the antecedent of كادوا.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p301/r6.anchor: أو قال الجن لقومهم: ذلك حكاية عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، وهذا كله مرتب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p301/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p301/r7.speaker: عاصم وحمزة وأبو عمرو
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p301/r7.claim: They read قل as a command to Muhammad, addressing the crowd, whether jinn or polytheists according to the interpretation of كادوا.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p301/r7.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وحمزة وأبو عمرو بخلاف عنه: قل: أي قل يا محمد لهؤلاء المزدحمين عليك

FARRA:v3p194/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p194/r2.speaker: الأعمش وعاصم
FARRA:v3p194/r2.claim: Al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim read “Say: I call upon my Lord.”
FARRA:v3p194/r2.anchor: قرأ الأعمش وعاصم : «قل إنما أدعوا ربي»

FARRA:v3p194/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p194/r3.speaker: عامة أهل المدينة
FARRA:v3p194/r3.claim: Most Medinan readers also read “Say: I call upon my Lord.”

FARRA:v3p194/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p194/r4.speaker: بعضهم
FARRA:v3p194/r4.claim: Some readers use the past-tense form qala, “he said.”

FARRA:v3p194/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p194/r5.speaker: بعضهم
FARRA:v3p194/r5.claim: Other readers use the imperative qul, “say.”

FARRA:v3p194/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p194/r6.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
FARRA:v3p194/r6.claim: A report from ʿAlī gives the reading “He said: I call upon my Lord.”
FARRA:v3p194/r6.anchor: عن أبي عبد الرحمن السلمي، عن علي بن أبي طالب- رحمه الله- أنه قرأها: (قال إنما أدعو ربي) .

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p243#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p243#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p243#2/r1.claim: Abu Jaafar, Asim, and Hamza read قل as a command; the others use قال, reporting that the Messenger said he calls only upon his Lord.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p243#2/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وعاصم وحمزة: "قل" على الأمر، وقرأ الآخرون: "قال" يعني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p243#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p243#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p243#2/r2.claim: Makkah’s unbelievers called Muhammad’s message tremendous and offered protection if he abandoned it; he answered that he calls only on his Lord.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p243#2/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل: وذلك أن كفار مكة قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: لقد جئت بأمر عظيم فارجع عنه فنحن نجيرك

NAHHAS:v5p52/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p52/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p52/r2.claim: The reading of qul innamā adʿū rabbī may be connected or begin a new clause; both senses are valid, and the following clause may also be coordinated or independent.
NAHHAS:v5p52/r2.anchor: ويقرأ ( قل إنما أدعو ربي ) والقراءة يقال متسقة ويقال منقطعة والمعنيان صحيحان

BIQAI-FULL:v8p195/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p195/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p195/r5.claim: The Prophet denies worshipping any partner alongside his Lord, including Wadd, Suwaʿ, and Yaghuth, whether an idol or a living being.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p195/r5.anchor: من ود وسواع ويغوث وغيرها من الصامت والناطق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384/r8.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384/r8.claim: The reading قال إنما, used by most of the Seven and Ali, supports identifying the servant as Noah.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384/r8.anchor: وقرأ جمهور السبعة وعلي بن أبي طالب: «قال إنما» ، وهذه قراءة تؤيد أن العبد نوح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384#2/r1.speaker: عاصم وحمزة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384#2/r1.claim: Asim and Hamza have the reading قل إنما, which supports identifying the servant as Muhammad, though either identity remains possible.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384#2/r1.anchor: «قال إنما» وهذه تؤيد بأنه محمد عليه السلام وإن كان الاحتمال باقيا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384#2/r2.claim: Readers differ on whether the yāʾ in ربي is opened or quiescent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384#2/r2.anchor: واختلف القراء في فتح الياء من ربي وفي سكونها

MUQATIL:72:15-23/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:72:15-23/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:72:15-23/r6.claim: Quraysh told Muhammad that his teaching was unprecedented and had made him enemies, then offered him their protection if he would abandon it; the verse directs him to call only on his Lord.
MUQATIL:72:15-23/r6.anchor: قالوا للنبى صلى الله عليه وسلم بمكة: إنك جئت بأمر عظيم لم نسمع مثله قط

TABATABAI:72:20-23/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:20-23/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:72:20-23/r4.claim: God commands the Prophet to explain that he calls upon God alone, resolving the audience's bewilderment at worship unlike anything they had seen.
TABATABAI:72:20-23/r4.anchor: أمر منه تعالى للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن يبين لهم وجه عبادته بيانا يزيل عنهم الحيرة

TABATABAI:72:20-23/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:20-23/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:72:20-23/r5.claim: The Prophet disavows the worldly schemes and tricks his audience suspects: he worships his Lord alone because worshipping one's recognized Lord is no cause for blame or surprise.
TABATABAI:72:20-23/r5.anchor: لست أريد بما آتي به من العمل شيئا من المقاصد التي تحسبونها وترمونني بها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p324/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p324/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p324/r1.claim: The ordinary reading has the Prophet say قال إنما أدعو ربي; Asim and Hamza instead read قل as a command, supported by the following command in 72:21.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p324/r1.anchor: أدعو ربي، وقراءة العامة: (قال) (¬5) إنما أدعو ربي (¬6). وقرأ عاصم، وحمزة: {قل} على الأمر (¬7)؛ لقوله بعده: {قل إني لا أملك لكم ضرا}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p324/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p324/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p324/r2.claim: Muqatil reports that Meccan unbelievers told the Prophet to abandon his extraordinary message and return to the old religion; the revelation of قل supports the imperative reading.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p324/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل: إن كفار مكة قالوا للنبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم-: إنك جئت بأمر عظيم لم نسمع مثله، وقد عاد الناس كلهم، فأرجع عن هذا.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p324/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p324/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p324/r3.claim: With the ordinary قال reading, the Prophet is understood to have answered their demand by saying that he calls only upon his Lord.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p324/r3.anchor: وهذا حجة لعاصم وحمزة. ومن قرأ: "قال" حمل هذا على أن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- أجابهم هذا لما قالوا له: جئت بأمر عظيم، قال:

ELMALILI:72:20-28/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:20-28/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:20-28/r1.claim: The Prophet is to say he invokes and worships only his Creator and Lord; opposition gives no reason for surprise or hostility, and he will not associate anyone with God or hope or fear in another.
ELMALILI:72:20-28/r1.anchor: ben ancak Rabbime dua ediyorum ve ederim yani neye öyle üzerime veya aleyhime keçeleniyorsunuz

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:20/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:20/r1.speaker: Mekkeli müşrikler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:20/r1.claim: The Meccan polytheists said they would protect Muhammad from his enemies if he abandoned the monotheistic message.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:20/r1.anchor: Mekkeli müşrikler, Hz. Peygamber’e, tebliğ ettiği tevhid dini yüzünden insanların düşmanlığını kazandığını, eğer bu davadan vazgeçerse kendisini düşmanlarına karşı koruyacaklarını söylüyorlardı

JISHUMI:v10p7119#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7119#2/r9.speaker: أبو جعفر، عاصم، حمزة
JISHUMI:v10p7119#2/r9.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, ʿĀṣim, and Ḥamza read the command ‘say, I only call upon my Lord’ without an alif; the others read it as a statement with an alif.
JISHUMI:v10p7119#2/r9.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وعاصم وحمزة: قل إنما أدعو بغير ألف على الأمر، وقرأ الباقون بالألف على الخبر.

STUDYQURAN:72:20/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:72:20/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:72:20/r1.claim: The Prophet’s exclusive call to his Lord answers Quraysh objections: they accused him of infringing on people and demanded he abandon his message.
STUDYQURAN:72:20/r1.anchor: I call only upon my Lord is a response to the objections of the Quraysh, who accused the Prophet of infringing upon the people

TABATABAI:72:18-20/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r1.claim: The verses derive the Prophet’s mission, divine oneness, and resurrection from the jinn story, then close by indicating the messenger’s protection from error.
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r1.anchor: في الآيات تسجيل للنبوة وذكر وحدانيته تعالى والمعاد كالاستنتاج من القصة وتختتم بالإشارة إلى عصمة الرسالة

BURSEVI:v10p153/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p153/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p153/r5.claim: The Prophet worships his Lord alone; this is no novel cause for astonishment or united hostility, and others should adopt the same state.
BURSEVI:v10p153/r5.anchor: فليس ذلك ببدع فلا مستنكر يوجب التعجب

TABRISI:72:19-20/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:19-20/r7.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:72:19-20/r7.claim: Muqatil says the opponents told Muhammad to abandon his unprecedented, momentous message; he was commanded to answer that he invokes only his Lord.
TABRISI:72:19-20/r7.anchor: وذلك أنهم قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إنك جئت بأمر عظيم لم يسمع مثله

TABRISI:72:19-20/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:19-20/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:72:19-20/r8.claim: The reply rejects associating anyone with God and supports the view that the preceding crowd is Quraysh pressing Muhammad to stop preaching.
TABRISI:72:19-20/r8.anchor: وهذا يعضد قول الحسن وقتادة لأنه كالذم لهم على ذلك

QASHANI:72:18-21/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:72:18-21/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:72:18-21/r5.claim: Calling only the Lord means affirming His oneness and turning away from everything else to avoid association.
QASHANI:72:18-21/r5.anchor: أوحده ولا ألتفت إلى ما سواه فأكون مشركا

BURHAN:v4p218/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p218/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p218/r2.claim: Some deny a negative use of إن and reconstruct deleted ما in examples such as ما إن الكافرون إلا في غرور; a poetic line supports the omission.
BURHAN:v4p218/r2.anchor: واعلم إن بعضهم انكر مجئ النافية وقال في الايات السابقة إن ما محذوفة والتقدير ما إن الكافرون إلا في غرور

KHATTABI:v1p40/r1.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p40/r1.speaker: المعترضون
KHATTABI:v1p40/r1.claim: Critics propose arranging sūras by subject—stories together, admonitions and parables together, and rulings elsewhere—for better organization, memorization, and clarity.
KHATTABI:v1p40/r1.anchor: قالوا: لو كانت سور القرآن على هذا الترتيب فتكون أخبار الأمم وأقاصيصهم في سورة , والمواعظ والأمثال في سورة

SAMIN-DURR:72:20/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:72:20/r1.speaker: عاصم وحمزة
SAMIN-DURR:72:20/r1.claim: ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read قل as an imperative, shifting to address the Prophet; others have قال, reporting the servant's speech.
SAMIN-DURR:72:20/r1.anchor: قرأ عاصم وحمزة " قل " بلفظ الأمر التفاتا أي: قل يا محمد. والباقون " قال " إخبارا

SAMIN-DURR:72:20/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:72:20/r2.speaker: الجحدري
SAMIN-DURR:72:20/r2.claim: Al-Jaḥdarī says the manuscript has قال; the imperative has parallels in قل سبحان ربي, al-Anbiyāʾ, and al-Muʾminūn.
SAMIN-DURR:72:20/r2.anchor: قال الجحدري: وهي في المصحف كذلك، وقد تقدم لذلك نظائر في قل سبحان ربي

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p333/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p333/r1.speaker: عاصم وحمزة
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p333/r1.claim: Asim and Hamza read قل without alif, while the others read قال with alif; Abu Amr is also reported with قل.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p333/r1.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وحمزة: قل إنما أدعو ربي [الجن/ 20] بغير ألف، وقرأ الباقون: قال

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p333#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p333#2/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p333#2/r1.claim: The قال reading continues the preceding third-person narration; the imperative قل fits the repeated second-person commands in verses 21–22.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p333#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو علي: وجه من قال أن ذكر الغيبة قد تقدم، وهو قوله:

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p333#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p333#2/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p333#2/r2.claim: The imperative also fits the following repeated commands: قل إنني لا أملك لكم ضرا ولا رشدا and قل إنني لن يجيرني من الله أحد.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p333#2/r2.anchor: ومن قال: قل فلأن بعده مثله وهو قوله: قل إنني لا أملك لكم ضرا ولا رشدا [الجن/ 21]

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p354/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p354/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p354/r3.claim: Keeping the alif reports that the Prophet first obeyed the command and then tells of it; dropping it preserves God's direct imperative wording.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p354/r3.anchor: يقرأ بإثبات الألف على وجه الإخبار وبطرحها على الأمر

NASHR:v1p437/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p437/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p437/r1.claim: For a moving hamza preceded by yāʾ or wāw, readers who ease the corresponding category after alif apply transfer and assimilation whether the letter is intrinsic or added; the two faces extend to extra liaison forms, though analogy requires assimilation only.
NASHR:v1p437/r1.anchor: وبمقتضى إطلاقهم يجري الوجهان في الزائد للصلة نحو (به أحدا، وأمره إلى، وأهله أجمعين) والقياس يقتضي فيه الإدغام فقط

NASHR:v1p437/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p437/r2.speaker: أبو العلاء
NASHR:v1p437/r2.claim: Abū al-ʿAlāʾ alone extends easing to this category as if the hamza followed a vowel, disregarding the long letters; the author says this is unknown to reciters and grammarians.
NASHR:v1p437/r2.anchor: وانفرد الحافظ أبو العلاء بإطلاق تخفيف هذا القسم مع قسم الألف قبله كتخفيفه بعد الحركة، كأنه يلغي حروف المد

NASHR:v1p437/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p437/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p437/r3.claim: The author transfers the hamza with yāʾ and wāw, but assimilates it when they are plainly extra solely for lengthening or liaison, following Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ṣāʾigh.
NASHR:v1p437/r3.anchor: ولكني آخذ في الياء والواو بالنقل، إلا فيما كان زائدا صريحا لمجرد المد والصلة فبالإدغام

QIRAAT-ER:72:20:1#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:72:20:1#1/r1.speaker: tns
QIRAAT-ER:72:20:1#1/r1.claim: The past-tense qāla replaces imperative qul, changing the discourse from a command to a narrative report while leaving the quoted content unchanged.
QIRAAT-ER:72:20:1#1/r1.anchor: tns, mutawatir: Past-tense reading replaces the imperative قُلْ (qul)

ALUSI-FULL:v29p93#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p93#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p93#2/r1.claim: “I worship my Lord” means worship Him alone; this is neither novel nor a sound reason for people to marvel or unite in hostility against the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p93#2/r1.anchor: قل إنما ادعوا اعبد ربي ولا أشرك به في العبادة أحدا فليس ذلك ببدع ولا مستنكر يوجب التعجب

ALUSI-FULL:v29p93#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p93#2/r2.speaker: الأكثرون
ALUSI-FULL:v29p93#2/r2.claim: Most readers use the past form “qāla,” understood either as God quoting the Prophet’s words to the crowd or as the jinn recounting them to their people.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p93#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ الأكثرون قال على أنه حكاية منه تعالى لقوله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم للمتراكمين عليه أو حكاية من الجن له عند رجوعهم إلى قومهم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p93#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p93#2/r3.speaker: عاصم وحمزة وأبو عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v29p93#2/r3.claim: ʿĀṣim, Ḥamzah, and Abū ʿAmr in one transmission read the imperative “qul,” which fits the following wording.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p93#2/r3.anchor: وقراءة الأمر وهي قراءة عاصم وحمزة وأبي عمرو بخلاف عنه وأوفق لقوله سبحانه

BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r8.claim: Worshipping and invoking God alone is neither novel nor a reason for amazement or united opposition.
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r8.anchor: فليس ذلك ببدع ولا منكر يوجب تعجبكم أو إطباقكم على مقتي

BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r9.speaker: عاصم وحمزة
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r9.claim: ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read “قل” as a command to the Prophet, aligning it with what follows.
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r9.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وحمزة «قل» على الأمر للنبي عليه الصلاة والسلام ليوافق ما بعده

DURR-FULL:v8p307/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p307/r8.speaker: عاصم
DURR-FULL:v8p307/r8.claim: Asim reads the phrase qul innamā adʿū rabbī without an alif.
DURR-FULL:v8p307/r8.anchor: عن عاصم أنه قرأ {قل إنما أدعو ربي} بغير ألف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r6.claim: The declaration “I only call upon my Lord” explains what the preceding clause means by the Prophet calling upon God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r6.anchor: وجملة { قل إنما أدعو ربي ولا أشرك به أحدا } بيان لجملة { يدعوه }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r7.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r7.claim: Most readers use the past-tense qāla, making the statement explain the servant’s act of calling.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r8.speaker: حمزة وعاصم وأبو جعفر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r8.claim: Ḥamzah, ʿĀṣim, and Abū Jaʿfar read qul as an imperative; the sentence then begins afresh and continues the revealed instruction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r8.anchor: وقرأه حمزة وعاصم وأبو جعفر { قل } بدون ألف على صيغة الأمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r9.claim: On the imperative reading, the implied continuation is “it was revealed to me … then say: I call only upon my Lord”; it remains part of the revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r9.anchor: فهو من تمام ما أوحي به إليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r10.claim: The restriction means that the Prophet worships no one besides God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r10.anchor: لا أدعو غيره ، أي لا أعبد غيره دونه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r11.claim: The added denial of associating anyone with God reinforces the restriction and is separately stated to give it special emphasis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r11.anchor: تأكيدا لمفهوم القصر ، وأصله أن لا يعطف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r12.claim: Verses 21–23 begin a fresh address: after recounting hidden matters about followers and rejecters, the sūra turns to instructing the Prophet how to answer hostile opponents.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r12.anchor: هذا استئناف ابتدائي . وهو انتقال من ذكر ما أوحي به إلى النبي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p384/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p384/r1.speaker: عاصم، حمزة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p384/r1.claim: ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read the opening as an imperative: “Say, I only call upon my Lord.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p384/r1.anchor: قرأ عاصم وحمزة قل إنما أدعو ربي بغير ألف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p384/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p384/r2.speaker: الباقون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p384/r2.claim: The remaining readers use the past-tense report, “He said: I only call upon my Lord.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p384/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون قال على الخبر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p384/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p384/r3.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p384/r3.claim: The Meccan disbelievers told the Prophet he had brought an unprecedented, grave matter and demanded that he abandon it; this verse was revealed in response.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p384/r3.anchor: قال مقاتل إن كفار مكة قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إنك جئت بأمر عظيم لم يسمع بمثله فارجع عنه فنزلت هذه الآية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r8.claim: The Prophet answers those who harmed, opposed, and rejected him and joined against him to defeat the truth: he worships his Lord alone, seeks His protection, and relies on Him alone.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r8.anchor: أي: قال لهم الرسول-لما آذوه (2) وخالفوه وكذبوه وتظاهروا عليه، ليبطلوا ما جاء به من الحق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r9.claim: The Prophet’s declaration means that he worships his Lord alone, without partner, and seeks refuge in and relies upon Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r9.anchor: أي: إنما أعبد ربي وحده لا شريك له، وأستجير به وأتوكل عليه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p633/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p633/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p633/r1.claim: The Prophet says this to those who gathered against him.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p633/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p633/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p633/r2.claim: One explanation is that the Prophet says he does nothing strange, only worships his Lord alone, and that this does not justify their united hostility.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p633/r2.anchor: يريد : ما أتيتكم بأمر منكر ، إنما أعبد ربي وحده

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p633/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p633/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p633/r3.claim: Alternatively, he says this to jinn gathered in wonder: worshiping and worshiping God alone is not strange; what is strange is invoking someone beside God and making Him a partner.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p633/r3.anchor: أو قال للجن عند ازدحامهم متعجبين : ليس ما ترون من عبادتي الله ورفضي الإشراك به بأمر يتعجب منه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p633/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p633/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p633/r4.claim: Alternatively, the words are spoken by the jinn to their people as a report of what the Messenger said.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p633/r4.anchor: أو قال الجن لقومهم ذلك حكاية عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p635/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p635/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p635/r1.claim: A prophetic report promises emancipation equal to the number of jinn who believed Muhammad or rejected him to whoever recites Sūrat al-Jinn.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p635/r1.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 1237 ) ( من قرأ سورة الجن

NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#5/r1.claim: The Prophet says that he invokes his Lord alone and associates no one with Him in worship.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#5/r1.anchor: وحده قال غير عاصم وحمزة ﴿ ولا أشرك به أحدا ﴾ في العبادة فلم تتعجبون

NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#5/r2.speaker: غير عاصم وحمزة
NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#5/r2.claim: The segment notes a reading difference involving readers other than ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah, but gives no distinct wording in this excerpt.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#5/r2.anchor: وحده قال غير عاصم وحمزة ﴿ ولا أشرك به أحدا ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#5/r3.claim: The statement challenges the jinn's amazement and crowding around the Prophet as he worships God alone.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:20-21/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:20-21/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:20-21/r5.claim: Most readers have indicative قال; Hamza and Asim read imperative قل.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:20-21/r5.anchor: وكذا قرأ أكثر القراء «قال» على ا لخبر

QURTUBI-FULL:72:20-21/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:20-21/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:20-21/r6.claim: Quraysh said Muhammad’s message made him everyone’s enemy and offered protection if he withdrew; this verse was revealed in response.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:20-21/r6.anchor: وسبب نزولها أن كفار قريش قالوا له: إنك جئت بأمر عظيم وقد عاديت الناس كلهم

QURTUBI-FULL:72:20-21/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:20-21/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:20-21/r7.claim: Muhammad says he invokes only his Lord and associates no one with Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:20-21/r7.anchor: وكذا قرأ أكثر القراء «قال» على ا لخبر

NASHR:v2p392/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p392/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر وعاصم وحمزة
NASHR:v2p392/r1.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, ʿĀṣim, and Ḥamza read qul without alif as an imperative; the others read qāla with alif as a statement.
NASHR:v2p392/r1.anchor: فقرأ أبو جعفر، وعاصم، وحمزة، قل بغير ألف على الأمر، وقرأ الباقون بالألف على الخبر
